questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The critical angle for a typical glass air interface is $42^{}^{\circ}$. If a ray of light falls normally on one of the faces of the prism of angle $45^{}^{\circ}$. The emergent ray will:
options: Will pass parallel to the second surface
Undergo total internal reflection from the second face
Will undergo refraction with a refracting angle $45^{}^{\circ}$
questions.solution:
Given critical angle $C = 42^{}^{\circ}$.

Angle of prism $A = 45^{}^{\circ}$.

Since the ray falls normally on the first face, the angle of incidence $i_1 = 0^{}^{\circ}$.

Thus, the angle of refraction at the first face $r_1 = 0^{}^{\circ}$.

Using the relation for a prism, $r_1 + r_2 = A$.

Substituting the values, $0^{}^{\circ} + r_2 = 45^{}^{\circ} \Rightarrow r_2 = 45^{}^{\circ}$.

The angle of incidence at the second face is $45^{}^{\circ}$.

Since $r_2 > C$ (45^{}^{\circ} > 42^{}^{\circ}$), the ray will undergo total internal reflection at the second face.

Answer: Undergo total internal reflection from the second face$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The distance between the objective and eye piece of astronomical telescope in normal adjustment is 27 cm and its magnifying power is 8. What is the focal length of the objective lens?
questions.solution:
In normal adjustment of an astronomical telescope, the final image is formed at infinity. The length of the telescope tube is the distance between the objective lens and the eyepiece.

$L = f_o + f_e$

The magnifying power of the telescope in normal adjustment is given by:

$M = \dfrac{f_o}{f_e}$

Given that $L = 27 \text{ cm}$ and $M = 8$.

Substituting the value of $M$:

$8 = \dfrac{f_o}{f_e}$

$f_o = 8 f_e$

Substituting this relation into the equation for the length of the telescope:

$8 f_e + f_e = 27$

$9 f_e = 27$

$f_e = 3 \text{ cm}$

Now the focal length of the objective lens, $f_o$:

$f_o = 8 f_e$

$f_o = 8 \times 3$

$f_o = 24 \text{ cm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The ratio of the angle of deviation produced by a thin prism, when it is placed in air to the angle of deviation produced when it is immersed in water of refractive index $\dfrac{4}{3} is:$
questions.solution:
The angle of deviation produced by a thin prism is given by $\delta = (\mu_{rel} - 1)A$, where $\mu_{rel}$ is the refractive index of the prism relative to the surrounding medium.

Assuming the refractive index of the glass prism to be $\mu_g = \dfrac{3}{2}$.

When the prism is in air, the relative refractive index is $\mu_g$.

$\delta_{air} = \left(\mu_g - 1\right)A = \left(\dfrac{3}{2} - 1\right)A = \dfrac{A}{2}$

When the prism is immersed in water, the relative refractive index is $\mu_{rel} = \dfrac{\mu_g}{\mu_w}$.

Given $\mu_w = \dfrac{4}{3}$, we have $\mu_{rel} = \dfrac{3/2}{4/3} = \dfrac{9}{8}$.

$\delta_{water} = \left(\dfrac{9}{8} - 1\right)A = \dfrac{A}{8}$

The ratio of the angle of deviation in air to that in water is:

$\dfrac{\delta_{air}}{\delta_{water}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{A}{2}}{\dfrac{A}{8}} = 4$

Thus, the ratio is $4:1$.

Answer: $4:1$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An object placed 40 cm in front of a thin convex lens is moved to 60 cm from the lens. If the focal length of the lens is 30 cm the ratio of magnification of the image at the initial position to the final position is:
questions.solution:
Using the lens formula, the magnification produced by a lens is given by $m = \dfrac{f}{f + u}$.

For the initial position, the object distance is $u_1 = -40$ cm and the focal length is $f = 30$ cm.

$m_1 = \dfrac{30}{30 + (-40)} = \dfrac{30}{-10} = -3$

For the final position, the object distance is $u_2 = -60$ cm.

$m_2 = \dfrac{30}{30 + (-60)} = \dfrac{30}{-30} = -1$

The ratio of the magnification at the initial position to the final position is:

$\dfrac{m_1}{m_2} = \dfrac{-3}{-1} = \dfrac{3}{1}$

Thus, the required ratio is $3:1$.

Answer: $3:1$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A glass slab of 16 cm thickness has its bottom surface silvered. An air bubble is located inside the glass slab at a distance of 8 cm from the top surface. The refractive index of glass is 1.6. Which of the following correctly represents the number of images seen by an observer looking vertically downwards from air onto the top surface?
options: Only one image is seen at a depth of 5 cm
Multiple images are formed due to multiple reflections and refractions
Only one image is seen at a depth of 16 cm
Two images are seen at depths 5cm and 15 cm
questions.solution:
The observer will see two primary images of the air bubble.

The first image is formed by the direct refraction of light from the bubble through the top surface of the glass slab.
Real depth of the bubble from the top surface, $x_1 = 8$ cm.
Apparent depth of the first image, $d_1 = \dfrac{x_1}{\mu} = \dfrac{8}{1.6} = 5$ cm.

The second image is formed by the light that travels downwards, reflects from the silvered bottom surface, and then refracts out through the top surface.
Distance of the bubble from the bottom silvered surface = $16 - 8 = 8$ cm.
The silvered bottom acts as a plane mirror and forms an image of the bubble at a distance of $8$ cm behind it.
Total real depth of this reflected image from the top surface, $x_2 = 16 + 8 = 24$ cm.
Apparent depth of the second image, $d_2 = \dfrac{x_2}{\mu} = \dfrac{24}{1.6} = 15$ cm.

Thus, two images are seen at depths of $5$ cm and $15$ cm.

Answer: Two images are seen at depths 5cm and 15 cm

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If a clear liquid has a refractive index of 1.45 and a transparent solid has a refractive index of 2.9, then for total internal reflection to occur at the interface between the two media; which of the following is correct?
options: The ray must travel from transparent solid to liquid at an angle of 15°
The ray must travel from liquid to transparent solid at an angle of 45°
The ray must travel from transparent solid to liquid at an angle of 30°
The ray must travel from liquid to transparent solid at an angle of 60°
questions.solution:
For total internal reflection to occur, light must travel from an optically denser medium to an optically rarer medium.

The refractive index of the transparent solid is $\mu_1 = 2.9$ and that of the clear liquid is $\mu_2 = 1.45$. Since $\mu_1 > \mu_2$, the solid is the denser medium and the liquid is the rarer medium.

Therefore, the light ray must travel from the transparent solid to the clear liquid.

The critical angle $\theta_c$ is given by:

$\sin \theta_c = \dfrac{\mu_2}{\mu_1}$

$\sin \theta_c = \dfrac{1.45}{2.9} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$\theta_c = 30^{{}^{\circ}}$

Thus, the ray must travel from the transparent solid to the liquid at an angle of $30^{{}^{\circ}}$ (or greater) for total internal reflection to occur.

Answer: The ray must travel from transparent solid to liquid at an angle of 30°

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An object is placed at an unknown distance from a convex objective lens of focal length 8 cm. The objective lens forms a real image which acts as an object for a convex eyepiece of focal length 6.25 cm. The distance between the objective and eyepiece is 45 cm. The microscope is adjusted so that the final image is formed at the least distance of distinct vision (25 cm). Which of the following is correct?
questions.solution:
For the eyepiece, the final image is formed at the least distance of distinct vision, so $v_e = -25 \text{ cm}$.

Using the lens formula for the eyepiece:

$\dfrac{1}{v_e} - \dfrac{1}{u_e} = \dfrac{1}{f_e}$

$\dfrac{1}{-25} - \dfrac{1}{u_e} = \dfrac{1}{6.25}$

$-\dfrac{1}{u_e} = \dfrac{1}{6.25} + \dfrac{1}{25} = \dfrac{4}{25} + \dfrac{1}{25} = \dfrac{5}{25} = \dfrac{1}{5}$

$u_e = -5 \text{ cm}$

The distance between the objective and the eyepiece is $L = v_o + |u_e|$, where $v_o$ is the image distance for the objective lens.

$45 = v_o + |-5|$

$v_o = 45 - 5 = 40 \text{ cm}$

Using the lens formula for the objective lens:

$\dfrac{1}{v_o} - \dfrac{1}{u_o} = \dfrac{1}{f_o}$

$\dfrac{1}{40} - \dfrac{1}{u_o} = \dfrac{1}{8}$

$-\dfrac{1}{u_o} = \dfrac{1}{8} - \dfrac{1}{40} = \dfrac{5 - 1}{40} = \dfrac{4}{40} = \dfrac{1}{10}$

$u_o = -10 \text{ cm}$

The object distance is $10 \text{ cm}$.

The total magnification $m$ of the microscope is the product of the linear magnifications of the objective and the eyepiece.

$m = m_o \times m_e = \left(\dfrac{v_o}{u_o}\right) \times\left(\dfrac{v_e}{u_e}\right)

$m = $\left(\dfrac{40}{-10}\right) \times \left(\dfrac{-25}{-5}\right) = (-4) \times5 = -20$

The magnitude of the total magnification is $20$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An object is placed 25 cm in front of a fully silvered concave mirror of focal length 15 cm. A plane mirror is placed 35 cm behind the concave mirror on the side opposite to the object. The final image after reflection first from the concave mirror and then from the plane mirror is formed at:
options: 37.5 cm in front of the plane mirror
37.5 cm in front of the concave mirror
questions.solution:
For the first reflection from the concave mirror:
Object distance, $u = -25$ cm
Focal length, $f = -15$ cm

Using the mirror formula:
$\dfrac{1}{v} + \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}$

$\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{25} = -\dfrac{1}{15}$

$\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{25} - \dfrac{1}{15} = \dfrac{3 - 5}{75} = -\dfrac{2}{75}$

$v = -37.5$ cm

The first image $I_1$ is formed $37.5$ cm in front of the concave mirror.

Now, for the second reflection from the plane mirror:
The plane mirror is placed $35$ cm behind the concave mirror (on the opposite side of the object).
Thus, the total distance of the first image $I_1$ from the plane mirror is:
$d = 37.5 \text{ cm} + 35 \text{ cm} = 72.5$ cm

The plane mirror forms a virtual image $I_2$ at the same distance behind it. Therefore, the final image $I_2$ is formed $72.5$ cm behind the plane mirror.

To find the position of the final image from the concave mirror:
Distance from concave mirror = Distance of plane mirror from concave mirror + Distance of $I_2$ from plane mirror
Distance = $35 \text{ cm} + 72.5 \text{ cm} = 107.5$ cm

The final image is formed $107.5$ cm behind the concave mirror.

Answer: 107.5 cm behind the concave mirror

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A plano-convex lens made of refractive index 1.5 and having radius of curvature $\mathrm{R}=4 \mathrm{ cm}$ fits exactly into a plano-concave lens made of refractive index 1.3 and having the same radius of curvature $\mathrm{R}=4 \mathrm{ cm}$ such that their plane surfaces are parallel to each other. The focal length of the combination is:
questions.solution:
For the plano-convex lens ($\mu_1 = 1.5$), $R_1 = \infty$, $R_2 = -4$ cm:

$\dfrac{1}{f_1} = (1.5 - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{\infty} - \dfrac{1}{-4}\right) = 0.5 \times \dfrac{1}{4} = \dfrac{0.5}{4}$ cm^{-1}$

For the plano-concave lens ($\mu_2 = 1.3$), $R_1 = -4$ cm, $R_2 = \infty$:

\dfrac{1}{f_2} = (1.3 - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{-4} - \dfrac{1}{\infty}\right) = 0.3 \times \left(-\dfrac{1}{4}\right) = -\dfrac{0.3}{4}$ cm^{-1}$

Equivalent focal length:

\dfrac{1}{F} = \dfrac{1}{f_1} + \dfrac{1}{f_2} = \dfrac{0.5}{4} - \dfrac{0.3}{4} = \dfrac{0.2}{4} = \dfrac{1}{20}$ cm^{-1}$

$F = 20$ cm$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: What is the refractive index of a material of prism if the frequency of light wave in it is $3 \times 10^{14} \mathrm{ Hz}$. The wavelength of light in the material of prism is $8000 Å$.
questions.solution:
The speed of light in a medium is given by the product of its frequency and wavelength. Let $v$ be the speed of light in the material, $f$ be the frequency, and $\lambda$ be the wavelength.

$v = f \times \lambda$

Given $f = 3 \times 10^{14} \text{ Hz}$ and $\lambda = 8000 \text{ Å} = 8000 \times 10^{-10} \text{ m} = 8 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$.

$v = (3 \times 10^{14}) \times (8 \times 10^{-7}) = 24 \times 10^{7} \text{ m/s} = 2.4 \times 10^{8} \text{ m/s}$.

The refractive index $n$ is defined as the ratio of the speed of light in vacuum $c$ to the speed of light in the medium $v$. Taking $c = 3 \times 10^{8} \text{ m/s}$:

$n = \dfrac{c}{v} = \dfrac{3 \times 10^{8}}{2.4 \times 10^{8}} = \dfrac{3}{2.4} = \dfrac{30}{24} = \dfrac{5}{4} = 1.25$.

Answer: 1.25

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An incident ray is incident at an angle $53^{}^{\circ}$ on one face of a prism. It emerges at an angle of $67^{}^{\circ}$. The ray suffers a deviation of $46^{}^{\circ}$. The refractive index of the material of prism is:
questions.solution:
Angle of prism: $i + e = A + \delta$

$53° + 67° = A + 46°$

$A = 74°$

Using the prism formula:

$\sin e = \sin A\sqrt{\mu^2 - \sin^2 i} - \cos A \sin i$

Substituting values ($\sin 53° \approx 0.8$, $\sin 67° \approx 0.92$, $\sin 74° \approx 0.96$, $\cos 74° \approx 0.28$):

$0.92 = 0.96\sqrt{\mu^2 - 0.64} - (0.28)(0.8)$

$0.92 + 0.224 = 0.96\sqrt{\mu^2 - 0.64}$

$\sqrt{\mu^2 - 0.64} = \dfrac{1.144}{0.96} \approx 1.191$

$\mu^2 \approx 1.418 + 0.64 = 2.058$

$\mu = \sqrt{2.058} \approx 1.43$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A biconvex lens has two different refractive indices in different regions. The upper half has a refractive index 1.7 and the lower half has a refractive index 1.5. The radius of curvatures of the two surfaces are $R_1=15 \mathrm{ cm}$ and $R_2=-25 \mathrm{ cm}$. Image of a distant object will be formed at:
questions.solution:
The focal length $f$ of a lens is given by the lens maker formula: $\dfrac{1}{f} = (\mu - 1) \left( \dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2} \right).

For the upper half, the refractive index $\mu_1 = 1.7$. Given $R_1 = 15 $\text{ cm} and $ R_2 = -25 $\text{ cm}, the focal length $ f_1$ is calculated as:

\dfrac{1}{f_1} = (1.7 - 1) \left( \dfrac{1}{15} - \dfrac{1}{-25} \right) =0.7 \left( \dfrac{1}{15} + \dfrac{1}{25} \right) =0.7 \left( \dfrac{5 + 3}{75} \right) =0.7 \times \dfrac{8}{75} = \dfrac{5.6}{75}.

$ f_1 = $\dfrac{75}{5.6} \approx13.39 \text{ cm}.

For the lower half, the refractive index $\mu_2 = 1.5$. The focal length $f_2$ is calculated as:

\dfrac{1}{f_2} = (1.5 - 1) \left( \dfrac{1}{15} - \dfrac{1}{-25} \right) =0.5 \left( \dfrac{1}{15} + \dfrac{1}{25} \right) =0.5 \left( \dfrac{8}{75} \right) = \dfrac{4}{75}.

$ f_2 = $\dfrac{75}{4} =18.75 \text{ cm}.

Since the object is at infinity, the images are formed at the focal points of the respective halves, which are 13.39 \text{ cm} and 18.75 \text{ cm}.$

Answer: 13.39 cm and 18.75 cm

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A beam of light parallel to the principal axis of a concave and convex lens, first passes through the concave lens of focal length 0.5 m and then through the convex lens of focal length 1.75 m. If the lenses are placed 1.25 apart, which of the given statement is true?
options: The emergent beam will focus at 1.75 m on the principal axis.
The emergent beam will pass parallel to the principal axis.
The emergent beam will focus at 1.25 m on the principal axis.
The emergent beam will focus at 0.75 m on the principal axis.
questions.solution:
Let the focal length of the concave lens be $f_1 = -0.5$ m and the focal length of the convex lens be $f_2 = 1.75$ m. The distance between the lenses is $d = 1.25$ m.

A beam of light parallel to the principal axis incident on the concave lens will appear to diverge from its focus, which is at a distance of $0.5$ m in front of the concave lens. Thus, the virtual object for the convex lens is located at a distance $u = -(d + |f_1|) = -(1.25 + 0.5) = -1.75$ m from the convex lens.

Using the lens formula for the convex lens: $\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f_2}$.

Substituting the values: $\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{-1.75} = \dfrac{1}{1.75}$.

This simplifies to $\dfrac{1}{v} + \dfrac{1}{1.75} = \dfrac{1}{1.75}$, which gives $\dfrac{1}{v} = 0$.

Therefore, $v = \infty$. The emergent beam will be parallel to the principal axis.

Answer: The emergent beam will pass parallel to the principal axis.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The focal lengths of the objective and eyepiece of a compound microscope are 1 cm and 10 cm respectively. Length of the tube is 25 cm. If the final image is formed at infinity, the magnifying power of the microscope is:
questions.solution:
Given the focal length of the objective $f_o = 1$ cm and the focal length of the eyepiece $f_e = 10$ cm.

The length of the tube $L$ is the distance between the second focal point of the objective and the first focal point of the eyepiece. For a compound microscope, when the final image is formed at infinity, the distance between the objective and the eyepiece is $v_o + f_e$.

The tube length $L$ is given as $25$ cm. In the standard configuration where the final image is at infinity, the distance between the lenses is $v_o + f_e = 25$ cm. Since $f_e = 10$ cm, we have $v_o = 25 - 10 = 15$ cm.

The magnification produced by the objective is $m_o = \dfrac{v_o}{u_o}$. Using the lens formula for the objective, $\dfrac{1}{v_o} - \dfrac{1}{u_o} = \dfrac{1}{f_o}$, we have $\dfrac{1}{u_o} = \dfrac{1}{v_o} - \dfrac{1}{f_o} = \dfrac{1}{15} - \dfrac{1}{1} = \dfrac{1 - 15}{15} = -\dfrac{14}{15}$. Thus, $u_o = -\dfrac{15}{14}$ cm.

The magnification of the objective is $m_o = \dfrac{v_o}{u_o} = \dfrac{15}{-15/14} = -14$.

The magnifying power of the eyepiece for the final image at infinity is $M_e = \dfrac{D}{f_e}$, where $D = 25$ cm is the least distance of distinct vision. Thus, $M_e = \dfrac{25}{10} = 2.5$.

The total magnifying power $M = m_o \times M_e = -14 \times 2.5 = -35$. The magnitude of the magnifying power is $35$.

Answer: $35$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A ray of light is travelling from glass of refractive index $\dfrac{3}{2}$ to water of refractive index $\dfrac{4}{3}$. What is the minimum angle of incidence for which no light enters in to the water?
questions.solution:
The condition for no light to enter the water is that the angle of incidence must be greater than or equal to the critical angle $i_c$.

The critical angle $i_c$ is defined by the relation $\sin(i_c) = \dfrac{\mu_{rarer}}{\mu_{denser}}$.

Given the refractive index of glass $\mu_g = \dfrac{3}{2}$ and the refractive index of water $\mu_w = \dfrac{4}{3}$.

Since $\mu_g > \mu_w$, the light travels from a denser medium to a rarer medium.

Substituting the values into the formula:

$\sin(i_c) = \dfrac{\mu_w}{\mu_g} = \dfrac{4/3}{3/2} = \dfrac{4}{3} \times \dfrac{2}{3} = \dfrac{8}{9}$.

Therefore, $i_c = \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{8}{9}\right)$.

Answer: $i_c=\sin ^{-1}\left(\dfrac{8}{9}\right)$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When a body of refractive index $\boldsymbol{\mu}=\mathrm{1. 4}$ is put into a liquid, the body becomes invisible. What would be the refractive index of the medium?
questions.solution:
A body becomes invisible when placed in a liquid if the refractive index of the body is equal to the refractive index of the liquid medium. This is because there is no refraction or reflection at the interface between the body and the liquid, as the light rays pass through without changing their path.

Given the refractive index of the body $\mu_{body} = 1.4$.

For the body to be invisible, the refractive index of the liquid $\mu_{liquid}$ must satisfy the condition $\mu_{liquid} = \mu_{body}$.

Therefore, $\mu_{liquid} = 1.4$.

Answer: $\mu=1.4$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: What is the velocity of light in vacuum if the velocity of light in a medium of refractive index 1.2 is ' v ' $\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$ ?
questions.solution:
The refractive index $\mu$ of a medium is defined as the ratio of the speed of light in vacuum (c$) to the speed of light in the medium (v$).

$\mu = \dfrac{c}{v}$

Given that $\mu = 1.2$ and the velocity in the medium is $v$, we have:

$1.2 = \dfrac{c}{v}$

Solving for $c$, the velocity of light in vacuum:

$c = 1.2 \times v$

Answer: $(1.2 v) \mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A plano-convex lens made of refractive index 1.5 and having radius of curvature $\mathrm{R}=4 \mathrm{ cm}$ fits exactly into a planoconcave lens made of refractive index 1.3 and having the same radius of curvature $R=4 \mathrm{ cm}$ such that their plane surfaces are parallel to each other. The focal length of the combination is:
questions.solution:
For the plano-convex lens ($\mu_1 = 1.5$), $R_1 = \infty$, $R_2 = -4$ cm:

$\dfrac{1}{f_1} = (1.5 - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{\infty} - \dfrac{1}{-4}\right) = \dfrac{0.5}{4}$ cm^{-1}$

For the plano-concave lens ($\mu_2 = 1.3$), $R_1 = -4$ cm, $R_2 = \infty$:

\dfrac{1}{f_2} = (1.3 - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{-4} - 0\right) = -\dfrac{0.3}{4}$ cm^{-1}$

\dfrac{1}{F} = \dfrac{0.5}{4} - \dfrac{0.3}{4} = \dfrac{0.2}{4} = \dfrac{1}{20}$ cm^{-1}$

$F = 20$ cm$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An object of height $h$ is placed midway between $f$ and $2 f$ in front of a biconvex lens. A real inverted image is captured on a screen placed a little beyond $2 f$ on the other side of the lens. If the whole arrangement is immersed in water without disturbing the object, lens and the screen positions, then the new image formed will be
options: Magnified real inverted image on the same side of the lens where the object is placed
Diminished real inverted image on the other side of the lens between $f$ and $2 f$
Magnified real inverted image on the other side of the lens beyond $2 f$
Magnified virtual erect image on the same side of the lens where the object is placed
questions.solution:
The focal length of a lens in a medium of refractive index $n_m$ is given by the lens maker formula: $\dfrac{1}{f_m} = (\dfrac{n_l}{n_m} - 1)(\dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2})$.

Initially, in air ($n_m = 1$), the focal length is $f$. When immersed in water ($n_m = 1.33$), the refractive index ratio $\dfrac{n_l}{n_m}$ decreases, which increases the focal length $f_m$ of the lens. Let the new focal length be $f' > f$.

The object is placed at a distance $u$ such that $f < u < 2f$. Since the lens is now in water, the new focal length $f'$ satisfies $f' > f$. The object position $u$ now satisfies $u < f'$.

When an object is placed within the focal length of a convex lens ($u < f'$), the lens acts as a simple magnifier. The image formed is virtual, erect, and magnified, and it is formed on the same side of the lens as the object.

Since the screen is fixed at the original position beyond $2f$, and the image is now virtual and formed on the same side as the object, no real image will be captured on the screen.

Answer: Magnified virtual erect image on the same side of the lens where the object is placed

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A beam of incident parallel light falls on a diverging lens of focal length 20 cm in magnitude. If a converging lens of focal length 15 cm in magnitude is placed at a distance of 10 cm to the right of the diverging lens on the other side, then, the final image formed is:
options: Virtual and is at a distance of 40 cm to the right of the diverging lens.
Real and is at a distance of 40 cm to the right of the converging lens.
Real and is at a distance of 30 cm to the right of the converging lens.
Virtual and is at a distance of 30 cm to the right of the converging lens.
questions.solution:
For the diverging lens, the focal length $f_1 = -20$ cm. Since the incident light is parallel, the rays appear to diverge from the focus of the diverging lens located at $20$ cm to the left of the lens. The image formed by the first lens acts as the object for the second lens.

The position of this virtual object for the second lens is $10$ cm (distance between lenses) $+ 20$ cm (focal length of first lens) $= 30$ cm to the left of the converging lens. Thus, $u_2 = -30$ cm.

For the converging lens, the focal length $f_2 = +15$ cm. Using the lens formula $\dfrac{1}{v_2} - \dfrac{1}{u_2} = \dfrac{1}{f_2}$, we have $\dfrac{1}{v_2} - \dfrac{1}{-30} = \dfrac{1}{15}$.

Solving for $v_2$: $\dfrac{1}{v_2} = \dfrac{1}{15} - \dfrac{1}{30} = \dfrac{2-1}{30} = \dfrac{1}{30}$.

Therefore, $v_2 = +30$ cm. The positive sign indicates that the image is real and formed at a distance of $30$ cm to the right of the converging lens.

Answer: Real and is at a distance of 30 cm to the right of the converging lens.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In the normal adjustment of an astronomical telescope, the objective and eyepiece are 36 cm apart. If the magnifying power of the telescope is 8, find the focal lengths of the objective and eyepiece.
questions.solution:

Given $M = 8$, we have $\dfrac{f_o}{f_e} = 8$, which implies $f_o = 8f_e$.

Substituting $f_o = 8f_e$ into the first equation: $8f_e + f_e = 36$.

$9f_e = 36 \Rightarrow f_e = 4 \text{ cm}$.

Then $f_o = 8 \times 4 = 32 \text{ cm}$.

Answer: $\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{o}}=32 \mathrm{ cm}, \mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{e}}=4 \mathrm{ cm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two light rays A and B travel from a medium into air at angles of incidence 15 degrees and 42 degrees respectively. In the medium, light travels 3 cm in 0.2 ns. Will there be total internal reflection? If so, which ray?
questions.solution:
The speed of light in the medium is $v = \dfrac{d}{t} = \dfrac{3 \times 10^{-2} \text{ m}}{0.2 \times 10^{-9} \text{ s}} = 1.5 \times 10^{8} \text{ m/s}$.

The refractive index of the medium is $n = \dfrac{c}{v} = \dfrac{3 \times 10^{8}}{1.5 \times 10^{8}} = 2$.

The critical angle $\theta_{c}$ is given by $\sin(\theta_{c}) = \dfrac{n_{air}}{n_{medium}} = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

Thus, $\theta_{c} = 30^{{}^{\circ}}$.

Total internal reflection occurs when the angle of incidence $i > \theta_{c}$.

For ray A, $i_{A} = 15^{{}^{\circ}} < 30^{{}^{\circ}}$, so no total internal reflection occurs.

For ray B, $i_{B} = 42^{{}^{\circ}} > 30^{{}^{\circ}}$, so total internal reflection occurs for ray B.

Answer: Yes, B

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A convex lens forms a real image of an object with magnification $m_1$. The lens is moved towards the object to obtain another real image of magnification $\mathrm{m}_2$. The image distance is increased by x. The focal length of the lens is
questions.solution:
For a real image by a convex lens, magnification $m = \dfrac{v}{|u|}$, giving $v = f(1+m)$.

Initial image distance: $v_1 = f(1+m_1)$
Final image distance: $v_2 = f(1+m_2)$

Given $v_2 - v_1 = x$:

$f(1+m_2) - f(1+m_1) = x$

$f(m_2 - m_1) = x$

$f = \dfrac{x}{m_2 - m_1}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A symmetric double convex lens is cut into two equal parts by a plane perpendicular to the principal axis. If the power of the original lens is 4D, the difference between the powers of the original lens and the cut lens is
questions.solution:
The power $P$ of a thin lens is given by the lens maker formula $P = (\mu - 1) \left( \dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2} \right)$. For a symmetric double convex lens, $R_1 = R$ and $R_2 = -R$.

Thus, $P = (\mu - 1) \left( \dfrac{1}{R} - \dfrac{1}{-R} \right) = (\mu - 1) \dfrac{2}{R} = 4$ D.

When the lens is cut into two equal parts by a plane perpendicular to the principal axis, each part becomes a plano-convex lens. For a plano-convex lens, one surface has radius $R$ and the other is flat, meaning $R_1 = R$ and $R_2 = \infty$.

The power of each cut lens $P'$ is $P' = (\mu - 1) \left( \dfrac{1}{R} - \dfrac{1}{\infty} \right) = \dfrac{\mu - 1}{R}$.

Comparing $P$ and $P'$, we see that $P' = \dfrac{1}{2} P$.

Given $P = 4$ D, the power of each cut lens is $P' = \dfrac{4}{2} = 2$ D.

The difference between the power of the original lens and the cut lens is $P - P' = 4 - 2 = 2$ D.

Answer: 2 D

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: One surface of a lens is convex and the other is concave. If the radii of curvatures are $R$ and $r$ respectively, the lens will be convex if
questions.solution:
The lens maker formula is given by $\dfrac{1}{f} = (\mu - 1) \left( \dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2} \right).

For a lens$ with one convex surface and one concave surface, let the radius of the convex surface beR_1 = R$ and the radius of the concave surface be $R_2 = r$. By sign convention, for a convex surface facing the object, $R_1$ is positive, and for a concave surface, $R_2$ is also positive if the center of curvature lies on the same side as the light direction.

The focal length $f$ is given by \dfrac{1}{f} = (\mu -$1) $\left( \dfrac{1}{R} - \dfrac{1}{r} \right)$.

For the lens to be convex (converging), the focal length $f$ must be positive. This requires $\dfrac{1}{R} - \dfrac{1}{r} \gt 0$.

Rearranging the inequality, $\dfrac{1}{R} \gt \dfrac{1}{r}$, which implies $R \lt r$.

Answer: $R \lt r$

questions.q: The radius of curvature of the curved surface of a plano-convex lens is 60 cm. If refractive index of the material of prism is 1.6 , then focal length of the lens is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Light enters at an angle of incidence in a transparent rod of refractive index '$n$'. The least value of '$n$' for which the light once entered into it will not leave it through its lateral face whatsoever be the value of the angle of incidence is
questions.solution:
Let the refractive index of the rod be $n$ and the refractive index of the surrounding medium be $1$. Let the angle of incidence at the end face be $i$ and the angle of refraction be $r$.

By Snell's law at the end face, $1 \times \sin(i) = n \times \sin(r)$.

The light travels inside the rod and hits the lateral surface at an angle of incidence $\theta = 90^{{}^{\circ}} - r$.

For the light not to leave the lateral surface, it must undergo total internal reflection. The condition for total internal reflection is $\sin(\theta) \ge \dfrac{1}{n}$.

Substituting $\theta = 90^{{}^{\circ}} - r$, we get $\cos(r) \ge \dfrac{1}{n}$.

Since $\sin(r) = \dfrac{\sin(i)}{n}$, we have $\cos(r) = \sqrt{1 - \sin^2(r)} = \sqrt{1 - \dfrac{\sin^2(i)}{n^2}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{n^2 - \sin^2(i)}}{n}$.

The condition $\cos(r) \ge \dfrac{1}{n}$ becomes $\dfrac{\sqrt{n^2 - \sin^2(i)}}{n} \ge \dfrac{1}{n}$, which simplifies to $n^2 - \sin^2(i) \ge 1$.

This must hold for any angle of incidence $i$. The worst case occurs when $\sin(i)$ is maximum, i.e., $\sin(i) = 1$.

Thus, $n^2 - 1 \ge 1$, which implies $n^2 \ge 2$, or $n \ge \sqrt{2}$.

The least value of $n$ is $\sqrt{2}$.

Answer: $\sqrt{2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: To a fish under water, viewing obliquely, a fisherman standing on the bank of a lake looks
options: Taller than what he actually is
Same height as he actually is
Taller or shorter depending on the refractive index of water
Shorter than what he actually is
questions.solution:
When a fish looks at an object outside the water, the light rays travel from the rarer medium (air) to the denser medium (water).

According to the laws of refraction, when light travels from a rarer medium to a denser medium, it bends towards the normal.

Let the height of the fisherman be $h$. The light rays coming from the top of the fisherman's head and his feet enter the water and bend towards the normal at the water surface.

Due to this refraction, the apparent position of the fisherman appears to be shifted upwards. Specifically, the rays appear to originate from a point further away from the surface than the actual object.

The apparent height $h'$ is given by $h' = \mu h$, where $\mu$ is the refractive index of water relative to air (\mu \approx 1.33$).

Since \mu > 1$, the apparent height $h'$ is greater than the actual height $h$.

Therefore, the fisherman appears taller than he actually is.

Answer: Taller than what he actually is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An object is placed at a distance of $12 \mathrm{ cm}$ from a convex lens on its principal axis and a virtual image of certain size is formed. If the object is moved $4 \mathrm{ cm}$ away from the lens, a real image of the same size as that of the virtual image is formed. The focal length of the lens in $\mathrm{cm}$ is
questions.solution:
Let $f$ be the focal length of the convex lens. The object distance is $u_1 = -12 \text{ cm}$. The lens formula is $\dfrac{1}{v_1} - \dfrac{1}{u_1} = \dfrac{1}{f}$.

For the virtual image, the magnification is $m_1 = \dfrac{v_1}{u_1} = \dfrac{v_1}{-12}$. Since the image is virtual, $v_1$ is negative, so $m_1$ is positive. Let the size of the object be $h$. Then the size of the image is $h_1 = |m_1| h = \left| \dfrac{v_1}{-12} \right| h = \dfrac{|v_1|}{12} h$.

When the object is moved $4 \text{ cm}$ away, the new object distance is $u_2 = -16 \text{ cm}$. The new image distance $v_2$ is positive because the image is real. The magnification is $m_2 = \dfrac{v_2}{u_2} = \dfrac{v_2}{-16}$. The size of the image is $h_2 = |m_2| h = \dfrac{v_2}{16} h$.

Given $h_1 = h_2$, we have $\dfrac{|v_1|}{12} = \dfrac{v_2}{16}$, which implies $v_2 = \dfrac{16}{12} |v_1| = \dfrac{4}{3} |v_1|$. Since $v_1$ is negative, let $v_1 = -x$ where $x > 0$. Then $v_2 = \dfrac{4}{3} x$.

Using the lens formula for both cases:
Case 1: $\dfrac{1}{-x} - \dfrac{1}{-12} = \dfrac{1}{f} \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{12} - \dfrac{1}{x}$
Case 2: $\dfrac{1}{4x/3} - \dfrac{1}{-16} = \dfrac{1}{f} \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{3}{4x} + \dfrac{1}{16}$

Equating the two expressions for $\dfrac{1}{f}$:
$\dfrac{1}{12} - \dfrac{1}{x} = \dfrac{3}{4x} + \dfrac{1}{16}$
$\dfrac{1}{12} - \dfrac{1}{16} = \dfrac{3}{4x} + \dfrac{1}{x}$
$\dfrac{4-3}{48} = \dfrac{3+4}{4x}$
$\dfrac{1}{48} = \dfrac{7}{4x}$
$4x = 48 \times 7 = 336 \Rightarrow x = 84$.

Substituting $x = 84$ into the first equation:
$\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{12} - \dfrac{1}{84} = \dfrac{7-1}{84} = \dfrac{6}{84} = \dfrac{1}{14}$.

Therefore, $f = 14 \text{ cm}$.

Answer: 14

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Figure below shows a lens of refractive index, $\mu=1.4$. $C_1$ and $C_2$ are the centres of curvature of the two faces of the lens of radii of curvature $4 \mathrm{ cm}$ and $8 \mathrm{ cm}$ respectively. The lens behaves as a
options: converging lens of focal length $12 \mathrm{ cm}$
diverging lens of focal length $20 \mathrm{ cm}$
converging lens of focal length $20 \mathrm{ cm}$
diverging lens of focal length $12 \mathrm{ cm}$
questions.solution:
The lens shown is a meniscus lens. We use the lens maker's formula: $\dfrac{1}{f} = (\mu - 1) \left( \dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2} \right).

For the given lens, the first surface (left) is convex towards the object space, so its center of curvature $ C_1$ is to the right. By sign convention, $R_1 = +4 $\text{ cm}.

The second surface (right) is also convex towards the object space, so its center of curvature $ C_2$ is also to the right. By sign convention, $R_2 = +8 $\text{ cm}.

Given $\mu = 1.4$, we substitute these values into the formula:

\dfrac{1}{f} = (1.4 - 1) \left( \dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{1}{8} \right)$

$\dfrac{1}{f} = 0.4 \times \left( \dfrac{2 - 1}{8} \right)

\dfrac{1}{f} =0.4 \times \dfrac{1}{8} = \dfrac{0.4}{8} = \dfrac{4}{80} = \dfrac{1}{20}

Therefore, $ f = +20 $\text{ cm}. Since the focal length is positive, the lens behaves as a converging lens.

Answer: converging lens of focal length 20 \mathrm{ cm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
When a biconvex lens of glass of refractive index 1.5 is dipped in a liquid, it acts like a plane sheet of paper.
This means the refractive index of the liquid is
questions.solution:
The lens maker formula is given by $\dfrac{1}{f} = (\mu_{rel} - 1) \left( \dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2} \right), where $\mu_{rel} = $\dfrac{\mu_{lens}}{\mu_{liquid}}.

When the lens acts like a plane sheet of paper, its focal length $ f$ becomes infinite, which implies \dfrac{1}{f} =0$.

Substituting this into the lens maker formula, we get $(\mu_{rel} - 1) = 0$, which means $\mu_{rel} = 1$.

Since $\mu_{rel} = \dfrac{\mu_{lens}}{\mu_{liquid}}, we have \dfrac{\mu_{lens}}{\mu_{liquid}} =1$, implying $\mu_{liquid} = \mu_{lens}$.

Given the refractive index of the glass lens is 1.5, the refractive index of the liquid must be equal to 1.5, which is equal to that of the glass.

Answer: Equal to that of glass

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A hollow prism is filled with water and placed in air. It will deviate the incident rays
options: Towards or away from the base
questions.solution:
A prism is a transparent medium bounded by two non-parallel refracting surfaces. When a light ray passes through a prism, it undergoes refraction at both surfaces.

According to Snell's law, when light travels from a rarer medium (air) to a denser medium (water), it bends towards the normal. When it travels from a denser medium (water) to a rarer medium (air), it bends away from the normal.

In a prism, the angle of deviation is determined by the geometry of the prism and the refractive index of the material. For any prism where the refractive index of the material is greater than the refractive index of the surrounding medium, the light ray is always deviated towards the base of the prism.

Since the refractive index of water (n \approx 1.33$) is greater than the refractive index of air (n \approx 1.0$), the hollow prism filled with water acts as a converging prism. Therefore, the incident rays are deviated towards the base.

Answer: Towards the base

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A telescope has an objective of focal length 60 cm and eyepiece of focal length 5 cm. The telescope is focussed for least distance of distinct vision for an object 300 cm away. The linear magnification produced by the telescope is:
questions.solution:
For objective lens: $f_o = 60$ cm, $u_o = -300$ cm

$\dfrac{1}{v_o} = \dfrac{1}{f_o} + \dfrac{1}{u_o} = \dfrac{1}{60} - \dfrac{1}{300} = \dfrac{4}{300}$

$v_o = 75$ cm

$m_o = \dfrac{v_o}{u_o} = \dfrac{75}{-300} = -\dfrac{1}{4}$

For eyepiece: $f_e = 5$ cm, image at $D = 25$ cm, so $v_e = -25$ cm

$m_e = 1 - \dfrac{v_e}{f_e} = 1 - \dfrac{-25}{5} = 1 + 5 = 6$

Total magnification: $m = m_o \times m_e = -\dfrac{1}{4} \times 6 = -1.5$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: For a $30^{{}^{\circ}}$ prism when a ray of light is incident at an angle $60^{{}^{\circ}}$ on one of its faces, the emergent ray passes normal to the other surface. Then the refractive index of the prism is:
questions.solution:
Given the prism angle $A = 30^{{}^{\circ}}$. The angle of incidence $i = 60^{{}^{\circ}}$. The emergent ray passes normal to the other surface, which means the angle of emergence $e = 0^{{}^{\circ}}$.

From the geometry of the prism, the angle of refraction at the first surface $r_1$ and the angle of incidence at the second surface $r_2$ satisfy $r_1 + r_2 = A$.

Since the emergent ray is normal to the second surface, $r_2 = 0^{{}^{\circ}}$. Therefore, $r_1 + 0^{{}^{\circ}} = 30^{{}^{\circ}}$, which gives $r_1 = 30^{{}^{\circ}}$.

Applying Snell's law at the first surface, $\mu = \dfrac{\sin i}{\sin r_1}$.

Substituting the values, $\mu = \dfrac{\sin 60^{{}^{\circ}}}{\sin 30^{{}^{\circ}}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}/2}{1/2} = \sqrt{3}$.

Answer: $\sqrt{3}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A ray of light travelling through a medium of refractive index $\dfrac{5}{4}$ is incident on a glass of refractive index $\dfrac{3}{2}$. Find the angle of refraction in the glass, if the angle of incidence at the given medium - glass interface is $30^{\circ}$.
questions.solution:
Given the refractive index of the first medium $n_1 = \dfrac{5}{4}$ and the refractive index of the second medium (glass) $n_2 = \dfrac{3}{2}$.

The angle of incidence $i = 30^{\circ}$.

Using Snell's Law, $n_1 \sin(i) = n_2 \sin(r)$, where $r$ is the angle of refraction.

Substituting the given values:

$\dfrac{5}{4} \sin(30^{\circ}) = \dfrac{3}{2} \sin(r)$

Since $\sin(30^{\circ}) = \dfrac{1}{2}$, we have:

$\dfrac{5}{4} \times \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{3}{2} \sin(r)$

$\dfrac{5}{8} = \dfrac{3}{2} \sin(r)$

$\sin(r) = \dfrac{5}{8} \times \dfrac{2}{3} = \dfrac{10}{24} = \dfrac{5}{12}$

Therefore, $r = \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{5}{12}\right)$.

Answer: $\sin ^{-1}\left(\dfrac{5}{12}\right)$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In the normal adjustment of an astronomical telescope, the objective and eyepiece are $32 \mathrm{ cm}$ apart. If the magnifying power of the telescope is 7, find the focal lengths of the objective and eyepiece.
questions.solution:
justment is given by $M = \dfrac{f_o}{f_e}$.

Given $M = 7$, we have $\dfrac{f_o}{f_e} = 7$, which implies $f_o = 7f_e$.

Substituting $f_o = 7f_e$ into the first equation: $7f_e + f_e = 32$.

$8f_e = 32 \Rightarrow f_e = 4 \text{ cm}$.

Using $f_o = 7f_e$, we get $f_o = 7 \times 4 = 28 \text{ cm}$.

Therefore, $f_o = 28 \text{ cm}$ and $f_e = 4 \text{ cm}$.

Answer: $f_o=28 \mathrm{ cm}$ and $f_e=4 \mathrm{ cm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When a particular wave length of light is used the focal length of a convex mirror is found to be $10 \mathrm{ cm}$. If the wave length of the incident light is doubled keeping the area of the mirror constant, the focal length of the mirror will be:
questions.solution:
The focal length $f$ of a spherical mirror is given by the relation $f = \dfrac{R}{2}$, where $R$ is the radius of curvature of the mirror.

The radius of curvature $R$ depends only on the geometry and the physical dimensions of the mirror surface. It is determined by the radius of the sphere from which the mirror is cut.

The focal length of a mirror is independent of the wavelength of the incident light. Changing the wavelength of the light does not alter the physical shape or the radius of curvature of the mirror.

Since the area of the mirror is kept constant, the radius of curvature $R$ remains unchanged. Therefore, the focal length remains $10 \text{ cm}$.

Answer: 10 cm

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A fish in water (refractive index $n$ ) looks at a bird vertically above in the air. If $y$ is the height of the bird and $x$ is the depth of the fish from the surface, then the distance of the bird as estimated by the fish is
questions.solution:

$d=(n-1) h$
where, $h=$ real depth $=y$
Now, apparent depth or the apparent height of the bird from the surface of the water $=y+(n-1) y=n y$. The total distance of the bird as estimated by fish is $x+n y$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: What will be the wave length, if a light of wave length 600 nm travels from air enters a medium of refractive index 1.5 and continues its journey through that medium?
questions.solution:
When light enters a medium, its frequency remains constant but wavelength changes. The new wavelength $\lambda'$ is given by:

$\lambda' = \dfrac{\lambda}{n}$

where $\lambda = 600$ nm (wavelength in air) and $n = 1.5$ (refractive index of medium).

$\lambda' = \dfrac{600}{1.5} = 400$ nm

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A person has a normal near point $25 \mathrm{ cm}$. What is the magnifying power of the simple microscope he used, if the focal length of the convex lens used is $10 \mathrm{ cm}$ and the final image is formed at the least distance of distinct vision?
questions.solution:
The magnifying power $M$ of a simple microscope when the final image is formed at the least distance of distinct vision $D$ is given by the formula:

$M = 1 + \dfrac{D}{f}$

Given values are:
Least distance of distinct vision $D = 25 \text{ cm}$
Focal length of the convex lens $f = 10 \text{ cm}$

Substituting these values into the formula:

$M = 1 + \dfrac{25}{10}$

$M = 1 + 2.5$

$M = 3.5$

Answer: 3.5

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When angle of incidence on one face of the equilateral glass prism is $3 / 4^{\text{th }}$ of the angle of prism, the ray of light undergoes minimum deviation. If the velocity of light in vacuum is '$c$' then the velocity of light in the glass is :
questions.solution:
For an equilateral prism, the angle of prism $A = 60^{{}^{\circ}}$.

The condition for minimum deviation is given by $i = e$ and $r_1 = r_2 = r = A/2$.

Given that the angle of incidence $i = \dfrac{3}{4} A$, we have $i = \dfrac{3}{4} \times 60^{{}^{\circ}} = 45^{{}^{\circ}}$.

Since $r = A/2$, we have $r = 60^{{}^{\circ}}/2 = 30^{{}^{\circ}}$.

Using Snell's Law at the first surface, $n_1 \sin(i) = n_2 \sin(r)$, where $n_1 = 1$ (air) and $n_2 = n$ (glass):

$\sin(45^{{}^{\circ}}) = n \sin(30^{{}^{\circ}})$

$\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = n \times \dfrac{1}{2}$

$n = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{2}} = \sqrt{2}$.

The refractive index $n$ is related to the velocity of light in vacuum $c$ and the velocity of light in glass $v$ by $n = \dfrac{c}{v}$.

Therefore, $v = \dfrac{c}{n} = \dfrac{c}{\sqrt{2}}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{c}{\sqrt{2}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A lens of power $+1 \mathrm{D}$ is made in contact with another lens of power $-2 \mathrm{D}$ the combination will then act as a:
options: converging lens of focal length $33.3 \mathrm{ cm}$
diverging lens of focal length $33.3 \mathrm{ cm}$
diverging lens of focal length $100 \mathrm{ cm}$
Converging lens of focal length $100 \mathrm{ cm}$
questions.solution:
The power of a combination of thin lenses in contact is given by the algebraic sum of the individual powers of the lenses: $P = P_1 + P_2$.

Given $P_1 = +1 \mathrm{D}$ and $P_2 = -2 \mathrm{D}$, the effective power $P$ is:

$P = 1 \mathrm{D} + (-2 \mathrm{D}) = -1 \mathrm{D}$.

The focal length $f$ of the combination is given by $f = \dfrac{1}{P}$ in meters.

$f = \dfrac{1}{-1 \mathrm{D}} = -1 \mathrm{m} = -100 \mathrm{cm}$.

questions.q: A fish in water (refractive index $n$ ) looks at a bird vertically above in the air. If $y$ is the height of the bird and $x$ is the depth of the fish from the surface, then the distance of the bird as estimated by the fish is
questions.solution:
The fish is at a depth $x$ below the water surface. The bird is at a height $y$ above the water surface.

When an observer in a medium of refractive index $n_1$ looks at an object in a medium of refractive index $n_2$, the apparent depth or height is given by the formula $d_{apparent} = d_{actual} \times \dfrac{n_{observer}}{n_{object}}$.

Here, the fish is the observer in water (refractive index $n$) and the bird is the object in air (refractive index $1$).

The actual distance of the bird from the surface is $y$. The apparent distance of the bird as seen by the fish from the surface is $y' = y \times \dfrac{n}{1} = ny$.

The total distance of the bird as estimated by the fish is the sum of the depth of the fish and the apparent height of the bird from the surface.

Total distance = $x + ny$.

Answer: $x+n y$

questions.q: A point object is placed on the optic axis of a convex lens of focal length $f$ at a distance of $2 f$ to the left of it. The diameter of the lens is $d$. An eye is placed at a distance of $3 f$ to the right of the lens and a distance $h$ below the optic axis. The maximum value of $h$ to see the image is
questions.solution:
The object is placed at $u = -2f$. Using the lens formula $\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}$, we have $\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{-2f} = \dfrac{1}{f}$, which gives $\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{f} - \dfrac{1}{2f} = \dfrac{1}{2f}$. Thus, $v = 2f$. The image is formed at a distance of $2f$ to the right of the lens.

The eye is placed at a distance of $3f$ to the right of the lens. Let the optic axis be the x-axis. The image is formed at $(2f, 0)$. The eye is at $(3f, -h)$.

The light rays from the image at $(2f, 0)$ must pass through the lens of diameter $d$ to reach the eye. The lens extends from $y = -d/2$ to $y = d/2$ at $x = 0$.

Consider the ray passing through the edge of the lens at $(0, d/2)$ and the image at $(2f, 0)$. The equation of this line is $y - 0 = m(x - 2f)$. Since it passes through $(0, d/2)$, we have $d/2 = m(0 - 2f)$, so $m = -d/(4f)$.

The ray equation is $y = -\dfrac{d}{4f}(x - 2f)$. At the eye position $x = 3f$, the height $y$ is $y = -\dfrac{d}{4f}(3f - 2f) = -\dfrac{d}{4f}(f) = -d/4$.

The eye is at a distance $h$ below the axis, so $h = |y| = d/4$. Any point further than $d/4$ below the axis will not receive light from the image formed by the lens.

Answer: $\dfrac{d}{4}$

The brightest image is formed by light that refracts into the glass, reflects from the silvered back surface, and refracts back out.

Refraction back out at front surface: Final apparent distance from front surface as seen in air:
$v' = \dfrac{v}{\mu} = \dfrac{19.5}{\dfrac{3}{2}} = 19.5 \times \dfrac{2}{3} = 13$ cm

$10f_e = 20 \text{ cm}$

\end{aligned}$ Hence, focus shifts to infinity.

questions.q: A convex lens of focal length $F$ is placed in contact with a concave lens of focal length $F$. The equivalent focal length of the combination is
questions.solution:
Given, $f_{1}=F$ and $f_{2}=-F$
The equivalent focal length of combination of two lenses is $\frac{1}{f}=\frac{1}{f_{1}}+\frac{1}{f_{2}}=\frac{1}{F}+\frac{1}{-F}=0 or f=\frac{1}{0}=\infty \quad \text{(infinity)}$

questions.q: A glass hemisphere of radius $0.1 \mathrm{ cm}$ and refractive index $1.5$ is placed over a spot on a table and the spot is viewed from above. The spot appears to be
options: $0.1 \mathrm{ m}$ above the top surface of the hemisphere
$0.1 \mathrm{ m}$ below the top surface of the hemisphere
$0.033 \mathrm{ m}$ above the top surface of the hemisphere
exactly on the top surface of the hemisphere
questions.solution:
Here, $R=-0.1 \mathrm{ cm}, \mu_{g}=15$
\therefore \quad u=-0.1 $\mathrm{ cm}$ From refraction formula, $\begin{aligned}& \frac{\mu_{a}-\mu_{g}}{R}=\frac{\mu_{a}}{v}-\frac{\mu_{g}}{u}\\
\Rightarrow \quad & \frac{1-15}{-0.1}=\frac{1}{v}-\frac{15}{(-0.1)} \quad\left(\because \mu_{a}=1\right) \\
\Rightarrow \quad 5 &=\frac{1}{v}+15 \\
\Rightarrow \quad v &=-\frac{1}{10}=-0.1 \mathrm{ cm}
\end{aligned}$ Here, negative sign shows that the image will be seen on the same size as that of object.
$\therefore$ The spot appears to be $0.1 \mathrm{ cm}$ below the top surface or exactly at the original position.
